definitions.meaning: a bowler is a hard round felt hat, so this is a kind of headgear
a game between two neighbouring rival teams

explanation.surface: A cricketer picked for a game against the neighbouring village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' wants to be a cricketer; here it is the hat. A local derby in Britain is a match between rival clubs from the same area.
explanation.definitionFit: The derby is the American name for the bowler hat, and a derby is also a sporting fixture between neighbouring rivals.

definitions.meaning: a guy is an informal word for a man or bloke
a person wielding an axe to cut down trees

explanation.surface: A man described as carrying an axe or a helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a fellow, a bloke, is spelt this way; and a lumberjack who fells trees with an axe is one too.

indicators.note: the phrase Temp has issues holds the run of letters within it, across its word breaks

explanation.surface: An office temp's problems involve workplace stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs inside 'tEMP HAS ISsues'; 'containing' tells you the phrase holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress laid on a word or idea is the weight or importance given to it, a synonym.

parts.note: reads like an invitation to step indoors, but 'come into' also means to receive property by bequest

explanation.surface: A friendly invitation to step indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: To come into money or property is to receive it when someone dies; the question mark flags the house as a legacy rather than a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into a property is to acquire it as heir under a will, the idiom for receiving a legacy.

indicators.note: going after places the word for occupy later in the answer than the fish

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
to enter a place is to go into and take it up, occupying it

explanation.surface: Someone heads off fishing and then takes over the local fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chippy' looks like a British fish-and-chip shop, which suits the fish; it is also slang for a carpenter, from wood chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is British informal slang for a woodworker, from the wood shavings the trade produces.

parts.note: to put someone off is to deter them
the setter speaking of something belonging to themself would say mine

explanation.surface: A setter's firm resolution is discouraged by something.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'setter's' means belonging to the compiler, so 'mine'.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve on a course is to decide it firmly, a synonym.

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
the van is the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A young woman is sitting at the front of a sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A low backless couch, a type of sofa or settee.

clue.text: Iran ends badly, losing energy, showing guts

indicators.note: the remaining letters are put together badly, in a new disordered sequence
losing means one letter is dropped from the words Iran ends

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A grim headline: Iran's campaign finishes poorly and the country runs out of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops the E (energy) from IRANENDS to leave IRANNDS, which 'badly' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts and innards both mean the internal organs, the entrails, so they are synonyms.

indicators.note: the opening letters of each of the four following words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: The first picture shown is either Jesus or a Christmas crib scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the initials of 'image Christ or nativity' spell the answer, and such a religious picture is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotional painting of Christ or the Nativity is the classic Orthodox religious image of this kind.

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for lout over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a slob is a lazy, uncouth lout
hie is an old word meaning hasten or go quickly

explanation.surface: An aggressive, cursing yob is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word qualifying 'lout'; it reverses SLOB. HIE is archaic for hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent means aggressively defiant; the British colloquial word for bloody-minded, uncooperative behaviour fits exactly.

clue.text: Tester is able to work before day's end

parts.note: can means is able to
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the end of the word day's is its final letter

explanation.surface: An examiner can get busy before the working day finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tester' looks like an examiner; it is an old word for the canopy over a four-poster bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is the overhead covering of a four-poster bed, a fabric roof suspended above it.

indicators.note: overturned means the word for cross is turned upside down, read backwards in an across light

parts.note: cross in the sense of annoyed is sore

explanation.surface: A deity's crucifix has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like the Christian symbol beside 'God'; it means angry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of love, a classical god.

indicators.note: eccentric means unconventional or odd, so these letters are laid out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone gives a silly smile to an odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninformed or lacking knowledge, which in loose use means foolish or dim.

indicators.note: violation suggests the letters are broken up and forced into another order

explanation.surface: An accusation that a law has been broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To make or enact statutes, as a parliament does, is to pass laws.

indicators.note: after puts the reworked letters later than the letter for right

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so the letters of please are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A political plea for reform, following the right wing's slump.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue's surface to the next one; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling back into a worse state after improvement is a decline, a synonym.

indicators.note: chasing puts the word for only behind, following the sailor in the down light

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
alone means only, solely

explanation.surface: A sailor pursuing nothing but fish and shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: An edible sea snail, a mollusc sold as food, also called ormer or paua.

indicators.note: the leader of the word Conservative is its first letter

parts.note: rosier means brighter or more hopeful

explanation.surface: A Tory leader's office workers become more optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees; it is a bishop's hooked staff. The ellipsis continues the previous clue's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's crook-shaped pastoral rod carried in ceremonies is this kind of staff.

indicators.note: under puts the word for shower below the holiday in the down light

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: A downpour on holiday beneath a pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to hold them back or prevent them, a synonym.

indicators.note: follows places the hip-hop artist after the abbreviation for with

parts.note: Eminem is a famous American hip-hop artist, an example of a rapper

explanation.surface: A famous hip-hop artist records a cover version of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' suggests a cover version of a song, fitting Eminem; it means packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper or plastic covering around a sweet or parcel protects its contents, a synonym.

parts.note: DI is detective inspector; the possessive adds S
a bloomer is a flower, and the aster is one

explanation.surface: A police detective's blunder ends in tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a British blunder, matching the detective; here it is a thing that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe or calamity, an awful event, is a tragedy.

clue.text: Disapproving sound you heard for short dress

parts.note: tut is the click of the tongue made in disapproval

indicators.note: heard means the word you is pronounced, giving a single letter with the same sound

parts.note: the letter U sounds just like the word you

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at you over a skimpy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's short stiff skirt, a brief costume dress worn for ballet.

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is heard as spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: something hideous to look at is a sight, a horror

explanation.surface: A gruesome scene staged for theatregoers.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sight' in British speech can mean an ugly mess: 'you look a sight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where something happens, its location or setting, is its scene.

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the phrase for vacant

parts.note: a property available for rent bears a sign saying to let
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Finding the best seat in an empty loo.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain TO LET marks a property for rent. 'Number one' is also child's slang for a wee, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavatory is a WC, a loo, so the two are synonyms.

definitions.meaning: to bury is to put a body in the ground
one of the two big clubs of Milan, the other being AC Milan

explanation.surface: Asking whether a club belongs to Bury, an English town, or Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the English town with its own football club; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a corpse in a grave, and Internazionale is Milan's famous football side.

indicators.note: dance means the letters jig about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting ready to throw yourself into slam dancing at a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly, very nearly, practically: the two phrases are synonyms.

indicators.note: around means the word for brew goes round the central letter

parts.note: a potion is a brewed drink, a concoction

indicators.note: the middle letter of afternoon is taken

explanation.surface: Serving a cup of tea halfway through the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-afternoon' gives R, the central letter of 'afternoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: A serving of food is a helping, an allotted share on the plate.

clue.text: Toss head of radicchio in casserole

indicators.note: in puts the leaf's initial inside the word for casserole

parts.note: a stew is a casserole, slow-cooked meat and vegetables

indicators.note: the head of the word radicchio is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cook throws some radicchio into the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss' suggests tossing salad leaves; it means to scatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter things carelessly about is to toss them around, a synonym.

clue.text: Fairy came across queen on edge

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology
met means came across, encountered
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A fairy came upon the queen at the edge of the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer boundary or border of an area is its edge, a synonym.
